title: Camp 2 close: the camel kneels
hook: he reaches Yathrib, where his camel kneels on a plot of land, a mosque is built, and the calendar begins again

segments.voice: Yesterday, the cave of Thawr. Your line was Allah is with us. Today, the last day of the stories.

For days, Yathrib has walked out to the edge of town every morning, watching the road from Mecca in the heat, and gone home disappointed. Then one day a lookout shouts: he's here. The whole town pours out. First he stops at Quba, just outside, and builds a simple mosque there, the first in Islam. In town, everyone wants him. Clan after clan grabs his camel's reins: stay with us. And he says, gently: let her go. She is under orders. The camel, al-Qaswa', walks on through the streets, the whole town following, holding its breath.
screen: `EVERY MORNING, WATCHING THE ROAD.` → `QUBA: THE FIRST MOSQUE.` → `LET HER GO. SHE IS UNDER ORDERS.`

segments.voice: Ibn Ishaq and Sahih al-Bukhari both tell where she knelt: an open yard where dates were laid out to dry, which belonged to two orphan boys. They offered it as a gift; he insisted on paying. There, carrying bricks with his own hands alongside everyone else, he built the mosque that, rebuilt and enlarged many times, still stands at the heart of the city. Yathrib got a new name: Madinat an-Nabi, the city of the Prophet, or simply al-Madinah, the city. Those who came from Mecca were the muhajirun, the emigrants; those of Medina who took them in, the ansar, the helpers. Years later, the Muslims began counting their calendar from this year, six hundred and twenty-two. Not from his birth, not from the cave. From the hijra, the year a community began. That's where the stories end, for now. Seventy-four days ago, on day twenty-two, you met Adam, the steward the angels questioned. Then Iblis who would not bow, and the garden with its one tree. Two sons. Nuh building on dry land. Ibrahim and the idols, the fire made cool, Hajar running between the hills, the House raised. Musa in a basket on the river, the fire on the mountain, the sea. Yusuf, from the well to forgive one old thing, out loud. Maryam, Zakariyya and Yahya, Isa by Allah's leave. Yunus in three darknesses. And then the Prophet ﷺ himself: an orphan in the desert, a trusted young man, a cave, one word, read, and a road out of Mecca. You know these stories now.
screen: `THE CAMEL KNEELS ON AN ORPHANS' YARD.` · `YATHRIB BECOMES AL-MADINAH.` · `THE CALENDAR BEGINS AGAIN.` · `FROM ADAM TO THE HIJRA.` · then, large: `YOU KNOW THESE STORIES NOW.`

segments.voice: Name the prophets you now know, one per breath: Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Musa, Yusuf, Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa, Yunus, Muhammad ﷺ, and any others you remember, with one picture each: a boat, a fire, a well, a palm tree, a fish, a cave. If you pray, you can add, peace be upon them.

Hijra, the migration from Mecca to Medina that started the Muslim calendar. Khalifah, Iblis, waswas, tawbah, khalil, Zamzam, Ka'ba, sabr jamil, nafs, Isa, yatim, amanah, iqra: the stories of the prophets, and then the Prophet.
Your line: you know these stories now. Tomorrow, camp three: how Muslims actually pray and live it. That's camp two, done.

howItsDone: Muslims date the Islamic year from the Hijra, and many visit the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, which stands on the land where his camel knelt; the first of Muharram marks the Islamic new year.

fork.setup: the Prophet rides into Yathrib, and every clan grabs his camel's reins, begging him to stay with them. what does he do?
options: let the camel go where she's led.
fork.reveal: let her go, she is under orders: the camel knelt on the orphans' yard, and the mosque was built there (Ibn Ishaq; Bukhari).

original.note: Arabic: the city; short for Madinat an-Nabi, the city of the Prophet.

trapdoor: what you thought: he arrived in Medina.
what it means: a hunted man arrived in a town that had waited for him, let a camel choose where to build, paid two orphans for the land, and a community began.
what a scholar hears: the Hijri calendar was set under 'Umar, counting year one from the Hijra rather than the birth or the first revelation.
